text:
REASON FOR REFERRAL
57-year-old man with ischemic heart disease (diagnosed 2022-09-03), coronary angiography 2022-09-21 and PCI 2022-09-24, who has not seen cardiology since his stent. Over the past three months he has had chest tightness on climbing two flights of stairs that settles within five minutes of rest, with no pain at rest. Routine referral.

CLINICAL QUESTION
Does he need stress testing or repeat angiography, and should his anti-anginal therapy change?

RELEVANT HISTORY
- Ischemic heart disease 2022-09-03; abnormal cardiac/coronary imaging finding 2022-09-21; angiography 2022-09-21; PCI 2022-09-24. Angiography and stent details are not in the extract.
- Kidney transplant 2023-08-14 after dialysis (2021-03-22 to 2023-09-04). On tacrolimus.
- Hypertension (1998), hyperlipidemia (2010), diabetic kidney disease with proteinuria, metabolic syndrome.
- Never smoked. No ED, inpatient or urgent care encounters in the last 24 months.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
Metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily, clopidogrel 75 mg, amlodipine 2.5 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, nitroglycerin 0.4 mg spray, simvastatin 20 mg (since 2022-09-10) and simvastatin 10 mg (since 2025-12-18), tacrolimus ER (Envarsus) 1 mg, Humulin 70/30 insulin, tramadol 50 mg. No allergies recorded. No aspirin is listed.

KEY RESULTS
- LDL: 113.7 mg/dL on 2025-12-18 (98.4 on 2024-12-18; 133.1 on 2021-12-07). HDL 42.1, triglycerides 187.5 on 2025-12-18.
- BP 107/53 and HR 68 on 2026-07-06. Systolic BP has been 92-107 since 2023.
- Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL and eGFR 124.7 on 2026-07-06; potassium 4.6 on 2026-07-06. Earlier values fluctuate widely (creatinine 3.0 on 2025-12-18, eGFR 86.6 on the same date).
- HbA1c 4.1% on 2026-07-06.
- Hemoglobin 17.1 g/dL on 2023-12-18, the latest on record.
- Ejection fraction and cardiac imaging: none recorded.

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
Angiography and PCI in September 2022, then clopidogrel, beta blocker, statin and sublingual nitroglycerin spray. No stress testing, echocardiogram or other cardiac imaging is recorded. The current symptoms have not yet been worked up.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
Renal transplant on tacrolimus (relevant to drug interactions, contrast exposure and statin choice). Insulin-treated diabetes (listed as prediabetes). Anemia listed as a problem, but the last hemoglobin was 17.1. Dependent drug abuse (onset 2018), chronic pain on tramadol, stress.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- No exam, ECG, or symptom detail beyond your note is in the chart. Add any exam findings, a current ECG, and whether symptoms are stable or worsening.
- Whether he has had any dyspnea, edema or other heart failure symptoms. The referral is labeled chronic heart failure, but no heart failure diagnosis, ejection fraction or echocardiogram is recorded.
- Details of the 2022 angiography and stent (vessel, stent type, residual disease) are not in the extract. Attach the reports if available.
- Duplicate simvastatin entries (10 mg and 20 mg) are both active. Confirm the actual dose. Also confirm whether he takes aspirin, and whether clopidogrel is still intended.
- Creatinine and eGFR values alternate between normal and severely abnormal. Confirm the current renal function with a recent result.
- HbA1c of 4.1% on insulin, with the indication listed as prediabetes, looks inconsistent. Confirm his diabetes status and hypoglycemia risk.
- Most recent labs and vitals are from 2026-07-06 and the lipid panel is from 2025-12-18. Consider updating lipids.
- The medication review is flagged as due.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
57-year-old man with ischemic heart disease, PCI 2022-09-24, now with 3 months of exertional chest tightness. It comes on climbing two flights of stairs and settles within 5 minutes of rest. No pain at rest. He has not seen cardiology since his stent. Routine.

CLINICAL QUESTION
Does he need stress testing or repeat angiography, and should his anti-anginal therapy change?

RELEVANT HISTORY
- Ischemic heart disease diagnosed 2022-09-03.
- Coronary angiography and cardiology consultation 2022-09-21, abnormal cardiac/coronary imaging recorded the same day.
- PCI 2022-09-24.
- No emergency, urgent care or inpatient encounters in the last 24 months.
- Never smoker (recorded 2026-07-06).

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
- Metoprolol succinate ER 100 mg daily
- Amlodipine 2.5 mg
- Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg spray as needed
- Clopidogrel 75 mg; no aspirin recorded
- Simvastatin, recorded as both 10 mg and 20 mg
- Lisinopril 10 mg
- Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg
- Tacrolimus ER 1 mg (renal transplant)
- Insulin 70/30 (Humulin)
- Tramadol 50 mg

No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
- BP 107/53, HR 68 on 2026-07-06. Systolic BP has been 92 to 107 since 2023.
- LDL 113.7 mg/dL on 2025-12-18, down from 133.1 on 2021-12-07. Triglycerides 187.5, HDL 42.1 on 2025-12-18.
- HbA1c 4.1% on 2026-07-06.
- Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, eGFR 124.7 on 2026-07-06. Creatinine was 3.0 on 2025-12-18 and has fluctuated between 1.1 and 3.4 since transplant.
- Potassium 4.6 mmol/L on 2026-07-06.
- Hemoglobin 17.1 g/dL on 2023-12-18, the last recorded value.
- BMI 28.5 on 2026-07-06.

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
No ECG, echocardiogram, ejection fraction or stress testing is recorded since PCI. No cardiac imaging reports are in the chart.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
- Kidney transplant 2023-08-14 after dialysis from 2021 to 2023 for diabetic kidney disease; on tacrolimus.
- Diabetic proteinuria.
- Hypertension, metabolic syndrome and hyperlipidemia.
- Chronic back and neck pain on tramadol.
- Drug dependence recorded 2018.
- Anemia listed as active.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- Heart failure: the referral condition lists chronic heart failure, but there is no heart failure diagnosis, ejection fraction or echo in the chart. Confirm or remove.
- Stent details: vessel, stent type and angiography findings from 2022 are not in the extract.
- Antiplatelet therapy: confirm clopidogrel monotherapy and whether aspirin was stopped or omitted.
- Statin: confirm the actual simvastatin dose, since 10 mg and 20 mg are both listed.
- Diabetes: insulin is recorded for "prediabetes" despite diabetic kidney diagnoses. HbA1c is 4.1%; check for hypoglycemia.
- Renal function: creatinine of 3.0 on 2025-12-18 versus 1.1 on 2026-07-06. Confirm current graft function.
- Recent results needed: vitals and labs are over 4 months old, and there is no CBC since 2023. Consider a current ECG, CBC and BMP.
- Drug dependence: specify the substance and current status (relevant if stimulant use).
- Symptoms: other symptoms (dyspnea, edema, orthopnea) and nitroglycerin use are not documented.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Routine review of ischemic heart disease with a stent placed in 2022. Over the past three months he has had chest tightness on climbing two flights of stairs, settling within five minutes of rest. No pain at rest. He has not seen cardiology since his stent.

CLINICAL QUESTION
Does he need stress testing or repeat coronary angiography, and should his anti-anginal therapy change?

RELEVANT HISTORY
Ischemic heart disease recorded 2022-09-03. Abnormal cardiac imaging and coronary angiography on 2022-09-21, with PCI on 2022-09-24. Stent details are not in the record. No MI, CABG or heart failure admission recorded. Hypertension since 1998 and hyperlipidemia since 2010. Kidney dialysis 2021-03-22 to 2023-09-04, then kidney transplant 2023-08-14. Never smoker (2026-07-06).

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
Cardiac: metoprolol succinate 100 mg ER (since 2022-09-10); clopidogrel 75 mg (since 2022-09-10); nitroglycerin 0.4 mg spray (since 2022-09-10); simvastatin 20 mg (since 2022-09-10) and simvastatin 10 mg (since 2025-12-18); lisinopril 10 mg, amlodipine 2.5 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg (all since 2026-07-06, for hypertension).
Other: tacrolimus ER 1 mg (since 2026-07-06); insulin isophane/regular 70/30 (since 2026-07-06); tramadol 50 mg (since 2026-07-06).
No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
BP 107/53 mmHg and HR 68 on 2026-07-06. Systolic has ranged 92 to 107 since 2023.
LDL 113.7 mg/dL on 2025-12-18 (133.1 on 2021-12-07; 89.7 on 2024-06-24). HDL 42.1, triglycerides 187.5, total cholesterol 192.3 on 2025-12-18.
Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, eGFR 124.7, potassium 4.6 on 2026-07-06. Creatinine was 3.0 on 2025-12-18.
HbA1c 4.1% on 2026-07-06.
Weight 92 kg, BMI 28.5 on 2026-07-06 (97.1 kg in 2023).
No echocardiogram, ejection fraction, stress test or other cardiac imaging recorded.
No ED, urgent care or inpatient encounters in the last 24 months.

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
Angiography and PCI in 2022. Current anti-anginal therapy is metoprolol and as-needed nitroglycerin; amlodipine was started 2026-07-06 for hypertension. No cardiac workup since 2022 is recorded.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
Prediabetes (1992). Diabetic kidney disease, microalbuminuria and proteinuria due to type 2 diabetes (2002 to 2020). Obesity. Anemia (1995). Chronic back and neck pain. Dependent drug abuse (2018, active).

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- Referral condition says chronic heart failure, but no heart failure diagnosis, ejection fraction or admission is in the record. Confirm or amend.
- Diabetes status: prediabetes is recorded, but so are type 2 diabetes kidney entries, and insulin was started for prediabetes. Clarify.
- Simvastatin 20 mg and 10 mg are both active. Confirm which he takes and the intended dose.
- No aspirin is recorded alongside clopidogrel. Confirm whether this is intentional.
- Symptom details not in the record: onset date, exertional limit, nitroglycerin use, adherence.
- Stent vessel and number, and the 2022 angiography report.
- Kidney status after the transplant, given the creatinine change from 3.0 to 1.1 between 2025-12-18 and 2026-07-06.
- Last hemoglobin was 2023. Recheck or confirm anemia status.
- Patient preferences about further testing.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Ms. Murphy, 55, has ischemic heart disease with PCI on 2023-09-12. About four months ago she stopped simvastatin 20 mg because of muscle aches and does not want to restart it. She is now on no lipid-lowering therapy, and her LDL was 139.5 mg/dL on 2025-09-03 while still prescribed simvastatin. Routine referral.

CLINICAL QUESTION
What lipid-lowering treatment do you recommend given statin intolerance?

RELEVANT HISTORY
- Ischemic heart disease diagnosed 2023-08-23.
- Coronary angiography 2023-09-05, followed by PCI 2023-09-12. Stent details and angiography report are not in our record.
- No chest pain since her stent.
- No emergency, urgent care or inpatient encounters in the last 24 months.
- Never smoker.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
- Clopidogrel 75 mg daily (since 2023-08-30)
- Metoprolol succinate ER 100 mg daily (since 2023-08-30)
- Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg spray as needed (since 2023-08-30)
- Hydrocodone 5 mg/acetaminophen 300 mg (since 2026-09-09, chronic neck pain)
- Simvastatin 20 mg: stopped by the patient about four months ago (still listed as active in our chart)
- No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
- LDL: 133.7 mg/dL (2022-08-17, before statin) and 139.5 mg/dL (2025-09-03, on simvastatin). There has been no lipid panel since she stopped.
- HDL: 30.5 mg/dL; triglycerides 124.6 mg/dL; total cholesterol 194.9 mg/dL (all 2025-09-03).
- HbA1c: 6.2% (2026-09-09), stable at 5.9 to 6.3% since 2017.
- Creatinine: rose from 0.8 mg/dL (2025-09-03) to 1.3 mg/dL (2026-02-18 and 2026-09-09).
- Potassium: rose from 4.2 mmol/L (2022-08-17) to 5.2 mmol/L (2026-09-09).
- BP 100/71 and HR 94 on 2026-09-09. HR was 75 to 80 in 2023 to 2026.
- BMI 28.7 (2026-09-09).

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
- Simvastatin 20 mg from 2023-08-30 until about four months ago. LDL did not fall meaningfully on treatment.
- No other statin, ezetimibe or PCSK9 therapy is recorded.
- No CK result is recorded.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
- Prediabetes since 2008, with a self-management plan.
- Chronic neck pain and chronic pain.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- The referral condition lists chronic heart failure, but there is no heart failure diagnosis, echocardiogram or ejection fraction in the chart. Please confirm or remove it, and add the EF if known.
- No aspirin is listed. Is she on single antiplatelet therapy with clopidogrel by design, or taking aspirin over the counter?
- Update the medication list to reflect that simvastatin was stopped, and give the stop date.
- Did muscle aches resolve after stopping? Was a CK checked? Have any other statins or doses been tried?
- LDL on simvastatin was essentially unchanged from the pre-statin value. Was adherence an issue?
- Consider a repeat lipid panel off statin before the visit.
- Creatinine and potassium have risen since 2025. Is there a known cause, and is repeat testing planned?
- Resting HR was 94 on metoprolol at the last visit. Is there any context for this?
- Any stent details (vessel, stent type) or an MI history to add?

REASON FOR REFERRAL
55-year-old woman with ischemic heart disease (diagnosed 2023-08-23) and a coronary stent (PCI 2023-09-12). She stopped simvastatin about four months ago because of muscle aches and does not want to restart it. She has had no chest pain since the stent. Her last LDL on file is 139.5 mg/dL (2025-09-03), measured before she stopped the statin. Routine referral.

CLINICAL QUESTION
What lipid-lowering treatment do you recommend given her statin intolerance?

RELEVANT HISTORY
- Ischemic heart disease, onset 2023-08-23. Abnormal cardiac and coronary imaging findings recorded 2023-09-05.
- Cardiology referral 2023-08-30. Coronary angiography 2023-09-05. PCI 2023-09-12.
- No emergency, inpatient or urgent care encounters in the last 24 months.
- Never smoked (2026-09-09). Prediabetes since 2008, HbA1c 6.2% on 2026-09-09 (6.0% on 2017-07-19).

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
- Metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily (since 2023-08-30)
- Clopidogrel 75 mg daily (since 2023-08-30)
- Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg spray as needed (since 2023-08-30)
- Simvastatin 20 mg, still listed as active but not being taken for about four months
- Hydrocodone 5 mg/acetaminophen 300 mg (since 2026-09-09)
- No allergies recorded. No ACE inhibitor/ARB or aspirin on the list.

KEY RESULTS
- LDL: 139.5 mg/dL on 2025-09-03 (133.7 on 2022-08-17, 142.7 on 2019-07-31). LDL has been above 130 on every reading, including after starting simvastatin in 2023.
- 2025-09-03: total cholesterol 194.9, HDL 30.5, triglycerides 124.6 mg/dL.
- Creatinine: 1.3 mg/dL on 2026-09-09, up from 0.8 on 2025-09-03 (1.3 also on 2026-02-18).
- Potassium: 5.2 mmol/L on 2026-09-09, up from 4.2 on 2022-08-17.
- BP 100/71, heart rate 94 on 2026-09-09. Systolic BP has drifted down from 120 (2017-07-19).
- BMI 28.7, weight 80.6 kg (2026-09-09).

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
Angiography and PCI as above. Treated with simvastatin 20 mg, clopidogrel and metoprolol since 2023-08-30. Simvastatin stopped by the patient about four months ago because of muscle aches. No other lipid-lowering agent is recorded.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
Chronic pain and chronic neck pain, with hydrocodone/acetaminophen started 2026-09-09. Medication review is flagged as due.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- No lipid panel since stopping simvastatin, and none since 2025-09-03. Consider repeating before the visit.
- Muscle aches: onset, severity, CK, and whether a different statin or lower dose was tried were not provided. Only simvastatin 20 mg appears in the chart.
- The referral lists chronic heart failure, but no heart failure diagnosis, ejection fraction or echocardiogram is in the chart. Please confirm the diagnosis and add any imaging.
- Stent details (vessel, number, date of DAPT plan) and the angiography findings are not in the extract. Clopidogrel is listed without aspirin, so please confirm the intended antiplatelet plan.
- Simvastatin is still marked active in the chart. Update it if she has stopped.
- Creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.3 and potassium to 5.2. Please confirm whether these are known or repeated.
- Please confirm no ACE inhibitor/ARB has been tried or contraindicated, given the low BP (100 systolic).
- Whether hydrocodone is related to the muscle aches or to any other issue is not documented.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Ms Justine Murphy is a 55-year-old woman with ischemic heart disease treated with PCI on 2023-09-12. She stopped simvastatin about four months ago because of muscle aches and does not want to restart it. She has had no chest pain since her stent. I would be grateful for your advice on lipid-lowering treatment. This is a routine referral.

CLINICAL QUESTION
What lipid-lowering treatment do you recommend given statin intolerance?

RELEVANT HISTORY
Ischemic heart disease first recorded 2023-08-23. Cardiology referral 2023-08-30 to 2023-09-05, coronary angiography 2023-09-05, PCI 2023-09-12. No emergency, inpatient or urgent care encounters in the last 24 months. Never smoked tobacco (2026-09-09).

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
- Metoprolol succinate ER 100 mg tablet
- Clopidogrel 75 mg tablet
- Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg/actuation mucosal spray
- Acetaminophen 300 mg / hydrocodone 5 mg tablet (since 2026-09-09)
- Simvastatin 20 mg (stopped about four months ago; still shows as active)
No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
- LDL 139.5 mg/dL, total cholesterol 194.9, HDL 30.5, triglycerides 124.6 (all 2025-09-03). LDL was 133.7 on 2022-08-17. No lipid panel since.
- HbA1c 6.2% (2026-09-09), 5.9% (2026-02-18).
- Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL (2026-09-09), 1.3 (2026-02-18), 0.8 (2025-09-03).
- Potassium 5.2 mmol/L (2026-09-09), 4.9 (2026-02-18).
- BP 100/71 mmHg and HR 94/min (2026-09-09). Systolic was 119 on 2023-08-23.
- Ejection fraction and cardiac imaging: none in the record.

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
Simvastatin 20 mg from 2023-08-30, stopped for muscle aches as above. No other lipid-lowering agent is recorded. No ACE inhibitor, ARB, diuretic or other heart failure therapy is recorded.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
Prediabetes (on a self-management plan), obesity, chronic neck pain, chronic pain, loss of teeth.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
1. The referral condition says chronic heart failure, but no heart failure diagnosis, echo or EF is in the record. Confirm whether to keep this.
2. Update the simvastatin entry to stopped, with the date.
3. Describe the statin intolerance: symptoms, CK, and any other statins or doses tried.
4. Add the most recent echo, angiography findings and stent details, if available.
5. Record prior MI or CABG status.
6. Last lipids were 2025-09-03, before simvastatin stopped. Consider repeating them.
7. Creatinine has risen to 1.3 and potassium is 5.2. Confirm whether these have been repeated or acted on.
8. Confirm whether the absence of ACE inhibitor/ARB and diuretic is intentional.
9. Add current symptoms other than chest pain, such as breathlessness or oedema.
10. BMI is 28.7 on the latest reading, but the findings list says "BMI 30+ obesity". Check which is current.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Urgent referral for an 85-year-old woman with known ischemic heart disease (CABG 2009) and chronic heart failure (EF 39.2% in 05/2025). Over the past two weeks she has had worsening breathlessness, now on walking across a room, with new bilateral ankle swelling. She is sleeping on three pillows. She had an ICU admission for heart failure in 11/2025.

CLINICAL QUESTION
[suggested - confirm] Does she have decompensated heart failure needing urgent reassessment (repeat echo, diuretic and GDMT optimization), and how should her regimen be managed given persistent low blood pressure and reduced eGFR?

RELEVANT HISTORY
- Ischemic heart disease 2009-08-17; CABG 2009-08-30. Clopidogrel, metoprolol, simvastatin and nitroglycerin spray started 2009-08-24.
- Chronic congestive heart failure, diagnosed 2025-04-27. NYHA assessment done that day (class not in extract).
- Emergency visit and ICU admission 2025-11-22 for heart failure; IV furosemide 2025-11-22 to 2025-12-06. Heart failure education 2025-12-07.
- Type 2 diabetes since 2004; CKD (stage 2 on problem list), microalbuminuria.
- Never smoked.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
Metoprolol succinate 100 mg and carvedilol 25 mg are both listed as active. Losartan 50 mg, furosemide 40 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, simvastatin 20 mg, nitroglycerin spray, metformin ER 500 mg, alendronate 10 mg. Furosemide, carvedilol, losartan, metformin and alendronate show start dates of 2026-11-09. No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
- LV EF 39.2% (echo 2025-05-26). No later echo.
- BP: systolic 85/46 on 2026-11-16; systolic 79 to 92 since 2026-09-21 (108/68 in 2017). HR 61 on 2026-11-09.
- NT-proBNP: 1963 (2025-04-27), peak 1869 (2025-12-02), 1584 (2025-12-06). None this year.
- eGFR 36.2, creatinine 1.4 on 2026-11-09 (eGFR 62.5 on 2026-10-19, 30.5 on 2026-06-29; 100.6 in 2017). K 4.5 on 2026-11-09.
- LDL 96.3 mg/dL on 2026-11-09 (range 85 to 145 this year). HbA1c 5.4% on 2026-11-09.
- Weight 77.6 kg, unchanged across all recorded values this year.
- Troponin I recorded as 0 on all readings through 2025-12-06.

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
Echo 2025-05-26, stress test 2025-04-27, ECGs 2025-04-27 and 2025-11-22, chest radiograph 2025-11-22 (reports not in extract). Heart failure telemedicine visits through 2026-11-16. No work-up for the current symptoms is documented.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
Proliferative diabetic retinopathy on anti-VEGF injections (latest 2026-09-28), diabetic neuropathy, osteoporosis, anemia.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- Clinical question was not given; the one above is suggested.
- Both metoprolol succinate and carvedilol are active; confirm whether this duplication is intended.
- Chart lists a hospice admission 2026-07-06 for heart failure, yet she is on active care. Confirm her current status and goals of care.
- Oxygen saturation is recorded as 79% on every reading in 12/2025; likely a data artifact. Please give a current value.
- Current examination findings, vitals, weight and any labs or ECG from this episode are not in the extract.
- NYHA class, echo report details and the CABG graft details are not available.
- Chart BMI/obesity finding (30+) conflicts with BMI 27.5.
- Medication review is flagged as due; no ACE inhibitor/ARNI, MRA or SGLT2 inhibitor is listed, and the reasons are not recorded.

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Urgent referral of Kam Harris, an 85-year-old woman with ischemic heart disease (CABG 2009-08-30) and chronic heart failure (LVEF 39.2% on 2025-05-26). Over the past two weeks her breathlessness has worsened, and she is now breathless after walking across a room. She has new bilateral ankle swelling and is sleeping on three pillows. Recent blood pressure has been persistently low (85/46 on 2026-11-16). She was admitted to hospice for heart failure on 2026-07-06.

CLINICAL QUESTION
[suggested - confirm] Please assess for acute decompensated heart failure and advise on management, including whether she needs admission. Please also advise how to optimize her heart failure regimen given her low blood pressure, declining renal function and hospice status.

RELEVANT HISTORY
- Ischemic heart disease from 2009-08-17. Abnormal cardiac imaging 2009-08-25. CABG 2009-08-30. No MI or PCI recorded.
- Chronic heart failure diagnosed 2025-04-27.
- ED visit and ICU admission for heart failure on 2025-11-22. She received IV furosemide from 2025-11-22 to 2025-12-06 and heart failure education on 2025-12-07.
- Urgent care visits on 2026-03-16, 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-12. Reasons are not recorded.
- Hospice admission 2026-07-06. Telemedicine heart failure follow-up since then, most recently 2026-11-16.
- Never smoked.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES
- Clopidogrel 75 mg daily (since 2009)
- Simvastatin 20 mg (since 2009)
- Metoprolol succinate ER 100 mg (since 2009)
- Carvedilol 25 mg (started 2026-11-09)
- Losartan 50 mg (started 2026-11-09)
- Furosemide 40 mg oral (started 2026-11-09)
- Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg spray as needed
- Metformin ER 500 mg and alendronate 10 mg
- No MRA or SGLT2 inhibitor recorded.
- No allergies recorded.

KEY RESULTS
- BP: systolic fell from 108 (2017-11-27) to 79 to 92 since 2026-09-21. Latest 85/46 (2026-11-16).
- HR: 61 (2026-11-09).
- NT-proBNP: 1963.1 (2025-04-27), 1584.4 (2025-12-06). None since.
- hs-troponin I: 0 on all 16 readings, 2025-04-27 to 2025-12-06.
- eGFR: fell from 100.6 (2017-11-27) to 36.2 (2026-11-09). Fluctuating, with 62.5 on 2026-10-19.
- Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL (2026-11-09).
- K: 4.5 mmol/L. Na: 141.3 mmol/L (2026-11-09).
- LDL: rose from 56 (2017-11-27) to 96.3 (2026-11-09). Peak 144.8 on 2026-06-29.
- HbA1c: 5.4% (2026-11-09).
- Hb: 12.2 g/dL (2025-12-06). None since.
- Weight: 77.6 kg (2026-11-09).

WORKUP AND TREATMENT TO DATE
- Stress test and NYHA assessment on 2025-04-27. Results and class are not in the extract.
- Echocardiogram 2025-05-26 showed EF 39.2%. No repeat since.
- ECGs on 2025-04-27 and 2025-11-22.
- Chest radiograph 2025-11-22.
- Report text is not available for any of these.
- Heart failure self-management plan in place.

OTHER RELEVANT CONDITIONS
- Type 2 diabetes with diabetic kidney disease and microalbuminuria. Proliferative retinopathy is on anti-VEGF injections; laser was done 2025-10-06. Neuropathy.
- Anemia.
- Hypertriglyceridemia.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE SENDING
- Hospice status and goals of care: is she still enrolled, and what are her and her family's wishes about admission, escalation and resuscitation?
- Both metoprolol succinate and carvedilol are listed as active. Please confirm which beta blocker she is actually taking.
- Losartan, carvedilol and furosemide were all started 2026-11-09 despite systolic BP in the 80s. Please confirm the doses and how she has tolerated them.
- Please add current vitals, weight trend, oxygen saturation and examination findings. Recorded weight has been unchanged at 77.6 kg since 2026-03.
- The problem list says CKD stage 2, but eGFR 36 fits stage 3b. Please also confirm whether metformin is appropriate.
- Oxygen saturation was recorded as 79% throughout the 2025-12 admission. Is this accurate?
- Why was no MRA or SGLT2 inhibitor used?
- What were the reasons for the 2026 urgent care visits?
- Do you want an NT-proBNP and hemoglobin drawn now?

REASON FOR REFERRAL
